passages.original: His verbis multorum hæreticorum denotat dogmata. Quamvis omnia , quæ vera non sunt, stulta dicenda siut ; alius tamen est, qui res fabulosas inducit, et alius qui calliditate tergiversationis rem veneno plenam proponit , ut est Arius et Photinus. Fahulosa autem non Lex, sed hæresis est, quantum ad tempus pertinet illud Judaeorum, dum quidam eorum sibi vindicarent praerogativam originum patriarcharum , quae de matrimoniis ortae sunt, cum ex hoc nullum I meritum sit apud Deum.
passages.english: With these words he marks out the doctrines of many heretics. Although everything that is not true must be called foolish, still, one man is he who introduces fabulous matters, and another he who with the cunning of evasion puts forward a matter full of poison, as are Arius and Photinus. Now it is not the Law that is fabulous but heresy, so far as concerns that time of the Jews, when some of them claimed for themselves the privilege of descent from the patriarchs, which arose from marriages, although from this there is no merit with God.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'siut' read as 'sint', 'Fahulosa' as 'Fabulosa'; the stray 'I' before 'meritum' is taken as a printing mark and omitted. 'originum' (literally 'origins') is taken as genealogical descent, following the lemma's 'originum enumerationes' (genealogies).
